requirements.name: backend-owned idle timer for codex app-server lifecycle
key UX: The backend tracks the last meaningful Codex activity time and treats the `codex app-server` process as idle only after a configured inactivity window elapses.

Meaningful activity includes session bootstrap that touches Codex, thread restore, new thread creation, turn start, turn streaming, pending-request traffic, and explicit thread actions such as interrupt, compact, fork, and rollback.
Simple frontend polling that does not require a live Codex roundtrip must not keep the process artificially awake forever.

requirements.name: safe shutdown guardrails that do not interrupt active work
key UX: Idle shutdown never happens while any turn is still in progress, while the backend is still receiving Codex stream events, or while unresolved pending requests still require the user to answer.
The backend only closes the `codex app-server` process after runtime state is settled enough that a later resume can reconstruct the session from saved thread data.
If the idle deadline arrives during active work, shutdown is deferred until the runtime returns to a safe idle state.

requirements.name: lazy restart on the next Codex-dependent action
key UX: When the process has been closed by the idle policy, the next action that actually needs Codex automatically starts a fresh `codex app-server` without asking the user to manually restart the backend.
Codex-dependent actions include restoring a thread, sending a new turn, creating a new thread, and invoking thread actions that require gateway access.
The restart path is backend-owned and reuses the same Codex command, working directory, and configured dynamic tool setup as normal server startup.

requirements.name: thread and session continuity across idle restarts
key UX: Idle shutdown does not delete thread identity, viewer tab ownership, or persisted thread history; it only releases the live `codex app-server` process.
After lazy restart, an existing thread can be resumed through the same bootstrap and `thread/resume` flow the product already uses for restored sessions.
If no thread existed before shutdown, the next send can still create a new thread normally instead of failing because the previous process was gone.

requirements.name: recoverable startup failure after idle shutdown
key UX: If on-demand startup fails, the user sees a normal actionable backend error instead of silent message loss or an endless loading state.
A failed wake-up keeps the current draft, selected workspace, and selected thread context intact so the user can retry.
The backend returns to a clean stopped state after startup failure so a later retry is not blocked by half-open gateway state.

requirements.name: configurable idle policy with default 10-minute timeout
key UX: The product defines one backend configuration value for the idle timeout duration in minutes so local operators can tune the shutdown policy without code changes.
When the idle-timeout setting is missing, the backend enables idle shutdown with a default timeout of 10 minutes.
If the idle-timeout setting is `0` or any negative number, the product treats idle shutdown as disabled and keeps the current always-on behavior.

requirements.name: dedicated configuration module for idle shutdown settings
key UX: Idle shutdown parameters are owned by a dedicated backend configuration module instead of being parsed inline across unrelated server startup files.
The module exposes a normalized idle-shutdown config shape so lifecycle code can consume one clear source of truth for enablement and timeout duration.
Invalid or disabled values are resolved once inside the config module, keeping the rest of the implementation free from repeated environment parsing branches.
